title: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave Will Get New Stories and Characters
summary:
Fans of the video game Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave have new content to look forward to. Nintendo and the game studio Intelligent Systems surprised players earlier this week by announcing an expansion pass for the game.

Fortune's Weave came out in September 2026 and has sold well and earned praise from critics, according to the gaming website Polygon. The expansion pass, which is available now on the Nintendo eShop, will add extra content in three waves.

The first wave adds four new weapons. The game calls them Prototypes, and they are based on special weapons from an earlier game in the series, Fire Emblem: Three Houses.

The second wave is expected during the 2026 holiday season. It will give four characters called Flame Lords new outfits, which players can switch back to the originals at any time. Other characters on a player's team can wear the outfits too. This wave will also let players use three powerful characters, the Dagdan gods Aurora, Smyrnos and Jurah, in the game's third part.

The third wave is the one many fans are most excited about. It will add four new story paths, called routes, about four rival lords named Anatolia, Talimun, Orchel and Bertrand. It is expected in 2027.

These routes connect to a change that some fans did not like. In an online question-and-answer session, Intelligent Systems said the game first had eight main characters, but the team cut it to four because that seemed too ambitious. Fans have been asking for the missing routes ever since the game came out.

Polygon suggested fan requests may have played a part, but said the routes were likely already being made and simply needed more time.
why_it_matters: The update shows how game makers can respond to what fans want after a game comes out, adding stories that were cut before release.

background_read: Fire Emblem is a long-running series of strategy video games made by the studio Intelligent Systems and published by Nintendo.
In these games, players move a team of characters across a battlefield map, taking turns like in a board game such as chess.
Many modern video games get extra content after release, often sold together as an expansion pass.
Fortune's Weave lets players follow different story routes, and the team cut its planned main characters from eight to four before release.
